headline: Islanders sign Ben Hutton to one-year contract
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Islanders signed Ben Hutton to a one-year contract, with a pro-rated $900,000 cap hit for the 2026-27 season. That is the extent of what the report gives us, and nothing in our data covers Hutton himself.

What we can say is where NYI stands. The Islanders are 7-5-2 with 16 points through 14 games, and so far this season they have produced 46.5 percent of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality that is usually a better guide to how a team is playing than the scoreboard. At five-on-five that share is an even 50 percent, so the gap comes from special teams and the overall number, not from their even-strength play. They have also scored 2.7 fewer goals than their chances suggest, while their goaltending has saved 10 more goals than expected, which is carrying a lot of the weight. With the power play creating 0.64 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.9, the margin for a depth move to matter is thin, but a team leaning this hard on its goalie can use any competent body on the blue line.
